Information about supported ROMs and Demulation features

• Widescreen battlefield view. • Touch selection, commands, construction and placement. • Touch-oriented right panel, radar navigation and fast camera centering. • Favorite units and structures with quick navigation and event alerts. • Manual saves, autosave and save-state previews. • Haptic feedback and Android-adapted menus and indicators. • Compatible modified-graphics overlays on top of the BASE ROM. • Original graphics, music, sounds, maps and game data are sourced directly from the selected ROM.

For Dune: The Battle for Arrakis, verified BASE ROMs are supported for USA (Genesis), Europe (Mega Drive), the German European release, and the Shedevr & Lipetsk Russian translation dated 02.08.2011. The user supplies their own ROM; Demulation verifies it and locally extracts the required original resources and data. A compatible mod ROM can be added separately as a source of modified graphics.
Demulation is not a universal console emulator: a supported game runs through natively recovered systems and rules while preserving the original gameplay mechanics.
Compared extracted resource packages with the immutable BASE resources. A package may include many sprites; byte differences do not necessarily mean a visible graphics change.

Choose a supported ROM with modified graphics. Demulation can replace only supported visual resources: terrain (sand, rock, dunes, spice and related map graphics), radar, and tactical graphics for units, buildings and effects. They replace the corresponding original resources from the main ROM. Text, scenarios and game logic from this ROM are never used.

The selected ROM is used only as a graphics source. Demulation compares supported resources with the original game and replaces only files that actually differ. Text, scenarios and game logic from this ROM are not used. Tap the ROM name below to choose another file.

Demulation is a specialized Android runtime environment for classic games, built through decompilation, analysis, and recovery of original software behavior. It is not a universal console emulator: instead of fully emulating the original hardware platform, each supported game runs through a natively recovered implementation of its systems and rules while remaining compatible with original data.
